explainedBy: The everyman sits by the filling tub: the rising water is a stock filling.

storyboard.claim: The rising bath water is, in systems terms, a stock filling.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman beside a bathtub filling from the faucet.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the bath the listener just pictured.
storyboard.addedInformation: Links the tub image to the word stock.

explainedBy: He points at the water piling up in the tub: a stock is an accumulation.

storyboard.claim: A stock is the foundation of any system: an accumulation.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same tub; the everyman now points at the water level.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; he points at the water.
storyboard.addedInformation: The definition is tied to the visible water level.

explainedBy: Pointing at the water: the water in the tub is the stock.

storyboard.claim: A stock is built-up material or information; the water in the tub is the stock.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same tub, the everyman pointing at the water, pleased he gets it.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Face turns to understanding.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: confirms the previous beat.

explainedBy: The everyman looks sadly at his wallet: a depleted checking balance is also a stock.

storyboard.claim: A depleted checking-account balance is a stock too.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman holding his wallet, disappointed.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From water to money: same idea, new stock.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows a stock can be money.

explainedBy: The everyman and his partner hold each other: the trust between them is a stock.

storyboard.claim: A reservoir, the trust you have in your partner, a brand's goodwill: all stocks.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman embracing his partner.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From money to an invisible stock: trust.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes trust a concrete relationship on screen.

explainedBy: The crucial overlooked point is about the tub: a stock changes only as fast as its flows.

storyboard.claim: It is an accumulation, and here is the crucial point we overlook.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The crucial overlooked point is about the tub: a stock changes only as fast as its flows.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Wraps the examples, sets up the rule. (fix round 1: bare figure -> named object/diagram)
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: setup line, text-led.

callout.text: Only as fast as its flows

explainedBy: The tub fills only as fast as the faucet pours: a stock changes only as fast as its flows allow.

storyboard.claim: A stock changes only as fast as its flows allow.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The bathtub alone, faucet in, drain out.
storyboard.onScreenText: Only as fast as its flows
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The rule, shown on the tub.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the stock is bound to its inflow and outflow.

explainedBy: Water goes from the faucet (inflow) into the tub (stock) and out of the drain (outflow).

storyboard.claim: The faucet pouring in is the inflow; the drain letting water out is the outflow.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A flow chain: faucet inflow -> water stock -> drain outflow.
storyboard.onScreenText: Faucet inflow / Water stock / Drain outflow
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Breaks the tub into its parts.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names inflow and outflow as the two flows.

explainedBy: The couple and the clock: trust cannot be refilled overnight, flows take time.

storyboard.claim: Stocks explain momentum: you cannot fix things overnight, a big source of frustration.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The couple and the clock: trust cannot be refilled overnight, flows take time.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Back to the couple; now trouble. (fix round 2)
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets up the trust example as a person-level story.

explainedBy: The partner glares at the everyman: ten years of lying have emptied her stock of trust.

storyboard.claim: After 10 years of lying, the stock of trust is completely empty.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The partner angry, facing the everyman.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same couple; the partner turns angry.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the empty trust as her anger toward him.

explainedBy: He reaches out with flowers to his still-angry partner: one weekend of good behavior does not refill the trust.

storyboard.claim: You cannot turn the good-behavior faucet on full blast for one weekend and expect the tub to be full.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman offering flowers; the partner still angry.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same couple; he tries to make up, she does not soften.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the inflow attempt and that the stock is still empty.

explainedBy: Flowers still in hand, he slumps by the clock: flows take time to accumulate into stocks.

storyboard.claim: It is physically impossible: it takes time for flows to accumulate into stocks.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman slumped with the flowers, a clock beside them.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same couple; his hope drops, time appears.
storyboard.addedInformation: Clock adds that time is the missing ingredient.

noVisual: "Shock absorber" and "memory of flows" are abstract; no icon reads as a buffer.
explainedBy: The tub's water level is the stock that absorbs shocks and remembers past flows.

storyboard.claim: Stocks act as shock absorbers: the memory of the history of changing flows.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The tub's water level is the stock that absorbs shocks and remembers past flows.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the trust story back to the general rule. (fix round 1: bare figure -> named object/diagram)
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: text-led.

noVisual: Decoupling of two flows has no drawable object.
explainedBy: Same tub: inflow and outflow need not match, the stock in between decouples them.

storyboard.claim: Stocks decouple inflow from outflow so they need not match; a real-world example follows.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same tub: inflow and outflow need not match, the stock in between decouples them.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same host; turns to the next example. (fix round 1: bare figure -> named object/diagram)
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: text-led.

explainedBy: A tree in the forest: the forest is a stock of living trees, refilled by new saplings.

storyboard.claim: The forest by a lumber mill is a stock of living trees; the inflow is saplings growing.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A tree in a forest.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: New example: forest.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the stock as trees.

explainedBy: The same forest: trees dying and loggers harvesting them are the outflow.

storyboard.claim: The outflows are trees dying and loggers harvesting them; the chainsaw is the outflow.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same tree, label for the outflow.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; names the outflow.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the chainsaw is not drawn; text carries it.

explainedBy: The harvested wood becomes the inflow into a new stock: cut lumber at the mill.

storyboard.claim: Logged wood becomes the inflow of a new stock, cut lumber at the mill; then a push-back.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same tree, label for the next stock.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; the outflow becomes a new stock.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: chaining of stocks only in text.

explainedBy: The everyman stares in alarm at the overfull tub about to flood the floor.

storyboard.claim: If the tub is about to spill over and flood the bathroom floor, it is a disaster.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman afraid beside the full bathtub.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Back to the tub for the push-back.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the overflow danger as alarm.

explainedBy: He reaches out to the faucet and the problem looks solved: the simple fix is turning off the inflow.

storyboard.claim: The fix is simple: reach out and turn off the faucet, problem solved, like a company burning cash.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same tub; the everyman reaches to the faucet, relieved.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; fear turns to a confident reach.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the faucet-only reflex as a physical act.

explainedBy: The CEO, coin in hand, just says 'Sell more' — pushing on the inflow.

storyboard.claim: The CEO does not look at accumulation; he looks at sales and says "Sell more."
storyboard.concreteVisual: The CEO, coin in hand, just says 'Sell more' — pushing on the inflow.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the bath to the company. (fix round 1: bare figure -> named object/diagram)
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows who reaches for the faucet in business.

explainedBy: We fix problems only by turning the faucet up or down: the tub shows the drain we ignore.

storyboard.claim: We fix problems by turning the faucet up or down; that is our biggest systemic blind spot.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same CEO with the coin: turning the faucet up or down is the blind spot.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same CEO; the host now judges the reflex. (fix round 1: bare figure -> named object/diagram)
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: blind spot carried by text.

explainedBy: The tub with its drain: the part we ignore is the outflow.

storyboard.claim: We ignore the drain; we are wired to obsess over inflows.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The bathtub, its drain visible.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the CEO back to the tub, now the drain.
storyboard.addedInformation: Points the viewer at the drain.

explainedBy: Hunter-gatherer brains hunt for a new source of food — the inflow feels like action.

storyboard.claim: Inflows feel like action; as hunter-gatherers our brains look for a new source of food.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Hunter-gatherer brains hunt for a new source of food — the inflow feels like action.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why we obsess over inflows. (fix round 1: bare figure -> named object/diagram)
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the search instinct as walking out to find more.

explainedBy: The everyman hurries out with his briefcase to earn more: we stare at the faucet.

storyboard.claim: Needing money, we get a raise, find a new oil field, hustle harder: we stare at the faucet.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman hurrying down the street with a briefcase.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Hunter instinct becomes the modern hustle.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows chasing inflow as rushing to work.

explainedBy: The tub fills just as well when the drain is plugged: decreasing the outflow fills the stock.

storyboard.claim: You can fill a stock just as effectively by decreasing the outflow, plugging the drain.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The bathtub and its drain.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The alternative to the faucet.
storyboard.addedInformation: States the other lever on the same tub.

explainedBy: The everyman slumps over his wallet: earning more is hard and depends on outside factors.

storyboard.claim: For a bigger bank account you can earn more, which is difficult and depends on external factors.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman slumped, holding his wallet.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the tub to his bank account.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the inflow route as a struggle.

explainedBy: Same man, same wallet, now relieved: spending less is within his control.

storyboard.claim: Or you can just spend less, which is in your control: the drain is easier to control.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same everyman with the wallet, now happy.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; worry turns to relief.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the drain option as the easy one.

explainedBy: An oil pump: billions are spent finding new oil, the inflow.

storyboard.claim: To prolong an oil economy we spend billions exploring and drilling for new oil: the inflow.
storyboard.concreteVisual: An oil pumpjack.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the household to the global scale.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the oil stock and the search for more.

explainedBy: Efficient engines burn less, which cuts the outflow and has the same effect on the oil stock.

storyboard.claim: Energy efficiency (engines burning less) cuts the outflow, same effect on the oil stock.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Flow: engines burn less -> less outflow -> oil in the ground.
storyboard.onScreenText: Engines burn less / Less outflow / Oil in the ground
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The drain side of the oil example.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes efficiency a cause -> effect on the stock.

explainedBy: The oil pump keeps getting the money: we overfund extraction and underfund efficiency.

storyboard.claim: We consistently underfund efficiency and overfund extraction.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The oil pumpjack again.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Back to the pump: where the money goes.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the favored side is the pump.

explainedBy: The everyman sags over his wallet: cutting the drain feels like sacrifice.

storyboard.claim: The faucet feels like progress; the drain feels like sacrifice. A psychological block.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman slumped with his wallet.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Why we ignore the drain.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the felt sacrifice of spending less.

explainedBy: The tub just fills or drains; it has no intent: the water level does not care about feelings.

storyboard.claim: The water level does not care about our feelings; the tub is not malicious.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The bathtub alone.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From feelings back to the neutral tub.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the no-malice point is text-led.

callout.text: The behavior is in the structure

explainedBy: The Slinky bounces by itself: the behavior lives in the structure, not the hand.

storyboard.claim: The behavior is in the structure.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The hand-held Slinky bouncing.
storyboard.onScreenText: The behavior is in the structure
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Ties the tub back to the opening Slinky image.
storyboard.addedInformation: Recalls the bounce-in-the-structure idea.

noVisual: Self-regulation of flows is only a question here; nothing yet to show.
explainedBy: The tub has no brain: how does it know when to stop filling?

storyboard.claim: How do systems regulate their flows on their own, without a brain?
storyboard.concreteVisual: The tub has no brain: how does it know when to stop filling?
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Next question. (fix round 1: bare figure -> named object/diagram)
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: question beat.

explainedBy: A freezing winter morning: the thermostat is the balancing loop that will fight the cold.

storyboard.claim: Systems use balancing loops; picture a freezing winter morning at a drafty desk.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A freezing, biting winter morning outside while he sits shivering.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: New scene for balancing loops. (fix round 1: bare figure -> named object/diagram)
storyboard.addedInformation: Puts the viewer in the cold room.

callout.text: A steaming mug of black coffee

explainedBy: He picks up a steaming mug of coffee and cups it in his hands.

storyboard.claim: In your hands you cup a steaming mug of black coffee.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same desk; he takes the mug.
storyboard.onScreenText: A steaming mug of black coffee
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; he takes the cup.
storyboard.addedInformation: Introduces the object of the loop.

explainedBy: Holding the mug, he worries: the heat escapes and the coffee cools.

storyboard.claim: Heat radiates away through your fingers; the coffee is inevitably cooling down.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same man, mug in hand, worried.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; comfort turns to concern.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the cooling as a change in face.

callout.text: A balancing loop has a target

explainedBy: The mug beside a target: the cooling coffee is a system seeking a goal.

storyboard.claim: That is a balancing loop: a system seeking a goal, always with a target.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same man with the mug; a target appears.
storyboard.onScreenText: A balancing loop has a target
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; the goal is added.
storyboard.addedInformation: Target makes goal-seeking literal.

explainedBy: The coffee's target is the room temperature around it.

storyboard.claim: The goal of the coffee system is room temperature; the bigger the gap, the faster heat flows out.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same man, mug, target.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same stage; names the target.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names what the target is.

explainedBy: The coffee starts at the boiling-hot end, far from room temperature, so heat rushes out.

storyboard.claim: Heat rushes out when it is boiling hot, far from room temperature.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Spectrum from boiling hot to room temperature, marker near boiling.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the cooling into a scale.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the gap that drives the fast cooling.

explainedBy: The marker nears room temperature and slows: the coffee homes in on equilibrium.

storyboard.claim: Closer to room temperature the cooling slows, homing in on equilibrium: nature's thermostat.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same spectrum, marker moved near room temperature.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same scale; the marker moves toward the goal.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the approach to equilibrium.

explainedBy: The wall thermostat: home heating is a battle between two competing balancing loops.

storyboard.claim: Your home thermostat is a classic balancing loop, really two competing ones.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The wall thermostat.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From coffee to the thermostat.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the device the next example is about.
